title: Inforcer raises $50M to help prepare smaller businesses for a new world of AI and security risks
excerpt: London-based Inforcer just closed a $50 million Series C round led by Insight Partners.
content_html:
London-based Inforcer announced Thursday a $50 million Series C round led by Insight Partners — the latest sign of investor interest in a category of startup solving a very mundane problem: Most small businesses can’t afford an in-house IT department, so they outsource it to managed service providers, or MSPs. Inforcer builds the software those MSPs use to manage all of their small- and medium-size business clients’ Microsoft 365 accounts from a single platform.

Companies like Inforcer have attracted increased VC interest due to growing market demand. Especially with AI and security risks, running an in-house IT department has become increasingly complicated, so more outfits are turning to MSP experts to handle it. But that also means MSPs need more infrastructure, not only to manage many more clients, but also to keep pace with how complex IT has become these days. 

No wonder, then, in just 18 months, Inforcer has raised three rounds totaling $110 million. Business has been growing 300% year-over-year, Inforcer co-founder and CEO Jamie Daum told TechCrunch, adding that the company has doubled its valuation between its Series B and C, though he declined to share that number. He said the near back-to-back rounds were needed because cyber threats and AI have continued to evolve rapidly. 

Thus far, the company, which launched in 2023, has invested much of its capital in product development, such as creating Shadow AI detection, to help organizations detect when employees are using unauthorized AI tools on company devices, and launching a threat detection and response tool to catch cybersecurity risks as they happen.

Cybersecurity, in particular, has become a growing area of concern, Inforcer co-founder and chief community officer William Connor told TechCrunch, noting that attacks now take minutes to execute rather than months to plan. Attackers, for example, are using AI to analyze what to attack in a company, while using LLMs to help craft more convincing phishing emails. 

“For SMBs, that means facing threats that are more automated, more scalable and harder to defend against than we’ve ever seen before,” Daum added. 

“Beyond hackers, there are also risks around how organizations are governing and protecting their company data, and governing the use of AI and agents within businesses,” Connor continued. “These are security concerns we are now planning around.” 

Inforcer is also looking to expand further in the U.S. With new products comes a slightly different business model. The 365 Manager was priced per client, but with the launch of the new threat-detection tool, Inforcer is moving toward a per-user model that better aligns with how MSPs sell these tools to their customers. “As we continue to move further into AI within our platform, some of our future products could also become consumption or token-based [pricing models],” Daum continued. 

Right now, the company says it will remain focused on the Microsoft suite, especially as so many SMBs still use it. They also aren’t particularly worried about Microsoft building more of these tools themselves, with Connor saying Microsoft’s focus has historically been on creating platforms for larger enterprises, leaving room for specialized vendors to serve smaller, more segmented customers.

“We see ourselves as complementary to Microsoft rather than competing with them,” Connor said. 

Other investors in the company include Dawn Capital and Meritech Capital.

content_html_zh:
总部位于伦敦的 Inforcer 周四宣布获得由 Insight Partners 领投的 5000 万美元 C 轮融资，这是投资者对解决一个非常平凡的问题的初创公司感兴趣的最新迹象：大多数小型企业无力承担内部 IT 部门的费用，因此他们将其外包给托管服务提供商 (MSP)。 Inforcer 构建了 MSP 用于从单一平台管理所有中小型企业客户的 Microsoft 365 帐户的软件。

由于市场需求不断增长，像 Inforcer 这样的公司吸引了越来越多的风险投资人的兴趣。 特别是在人工智能和安全风险的影响下，内部 IT 部门的运营变得越来越复杂，因此越来越多的机构开始寻求 MSP 专家来处理。 但这也意味着 MSP 需要更多的基础设施，不仅要管理更多的客户，还要跟上当今 IT 的复杂程度。

难怪在短短 18 个月内，Inforcer 就筹集了三轮融资，总额达 1.1 亿美元。 Inforcer 联合创始人兼首席执行官 Jamie Daum 告诉 TechCrunch，业务同比增长 300%，并补充说，该公司在 B 轮和 C 轮融资期间估值翻了一番，但他拒绝透露这一数字。 他表示，由于网络威胁和人工智能持续快速发展，因此需要进行近乎背靠背的几轮谈判。

到目前为止，这家于 2023 年成立的公司已在产品开发上投入了大量资金，例如创建 Shadow AI 检测，以帮助组织检测员工何时在公司设备上使用未经授权的 AI 工具，并推出威胁检测和响应工具以在网络安全风险发生时捕获它们。

Inforcer 联合创始人兼首席社区官 William Connor 告诉 TechCrunch，网络安全尤其已成为一个日益受到关注的领域，他指出，现在的攻击只需几分钟即可执行，而不是几个月的计划。 例如，攻击者正在使用人工智能来分析公司中要攻击的内容，同时使用法学硕士来帮助制作更有说服力的网络钓鱼电子邮件。

“对于中小型企业来说，这意味着面临比我们以前见过的更自动化、更可扩展且更难防御的威胁，”Daum 补充道。

康纳继续说道：“除了黑客之外，组织如何管理和保护其公司数据，以及如何管理企业内人工智能和代理的使用也存在风险。” “这些是我们现在正在计划解决的安全问题。”

Inforcer 还希望在美国进一步扩张。新产品的推出带来了略有不同的商业模式。 365 Manager 按客户定价，但随着新威胁检测工具的推出，Inforcer 正在转向按用户模式，以更好地符合 MSP 向客户销售这些工具的方式。 “随着我们继续在平台内进一步进军人工智能，我们未来的一些产品也可能成为消费或基于代币的[定价模型]，”Daum 继续说道。

目前，该公司表示将继续专注于微软套件，特别是因为许多中小企业仍在使用它。 他们也并不特别担心微软自己构建更多的此类工具，康纳表示，微软历来的重点是为大型企业创建平台，为专业供应商为更小、更细分的客户提供服务留下了空间。

“我们认为自己是微软的补充，而不是与他们竞争，”康纳说。

该公司的其他投资者包括Dawn Capital和Meritech Capital。
